<description>
Follow-up to #36164, as suggested in https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36164#issuecomment-5541268260.

Tracked in https://github.com/kevkevinpal/bitcoin/issues/550.

**Problem:** `MakeByteSpan` and `MakeUCharSpan` return views into their input. A temporary container can leave those views dangling.

**Fix:** Add `LIFETIMEBOUND` to the overload taking non-`borrowed_range` types, so Clang diagnoses the misuse on owning containers without flagging correct code that passes a view. `leveldb::Slice` is opted into `borrowed_range` so `dbwrapper` can keep using the helper. Matching the `util/string.h` helpers from #36164.
</description>

unrelated: Seems odd to require BasicByte here for MakeUCharSpan, but not for MakeByteSpan.

Either it should be removed for both, or enforced for both.

Maybe it can be made explicit with something like:

```cpp
#include <span>
#include <cstddef>

enum class EndianPolicy {
    Strict,
    Ignore
};

template <EndianPolicy Policy = EndianPolicy::Strict, typename V>
auto MakeByteSpan(const V& v) noexcept
{
    if constexpr (sizeof(typename decltype(std::span{v})::element_type) > 1) {
        static_assert(Policy == EndianPolicy::Ignore,
            "Cannot create byte span for multi-byte types: byte order is architecture-dependent. "
            "Use 'MakeByteSpan<EndianPolicy::Ignore>(...)' to acknowledge this.");
    }

    return std::as_bytes(std::span{v});
}
```

Also, UCharSpanCast is only called/used once, so maybe it can be renamed to `UCharCast`?

Afterwards, MakeUCharSpan(a) could even be removed and replaced by UCharCast(MakeByteSpan(a))?
